guidebook.intro: Telling stories. **Ndra’bo ndra’bo** (long, long ago) opens a tale; **Ma e’yo de nde** (my story ends here) closes it.

tips.title: Ndra’bo ndra’bo
body: **Ndra’bo ndra’bo, etu alu…** (once upon a time, one day…). **Agupi alu ovu ra** (there was a man).
**Ka vutia** (and then) moves the story on.

tips.title: Dria si
body: **Dria si** (in the end), **Ma e’yo de nde** (my story ends here).
Swahili storytellers call **Paukwa!** and listeners answer **Pakawa!**

culture.title: Evening stories
body: Lugbara children learn folktales around the evening fire, often about the clever hare and greedy hyena.
